subject: Career
title: Why Cover Letters Still Matter
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Why Cover Letters Still Matter.

hook.text: Many candidates skip the cover letter. That's exactly why writing one gives you an edge.

buildup.text: A Robert Half survey found 58% of hiring managers prefer candidates who include one.

discovery.text: The cover letter answers the question resumes can't: why this company, why this role, why now?

twist.text: A bad cover letter hurts more than none. Generic templates get spotted instantly.

climax.text: Three specific sentences beat three generic paragraphs. Be brief, be specific, be done.

punchline.text: A cover letter shows you cared enough to write one.

quiz.question: What question does a cover letter answer that a resume cannot?
options: Why this company, role, and timing

details.summary: Cover letters remain valuable because they provide context that resumes cannot: your motivation for applying, how your experience connects to the specific role, and your communication style. They differentiate you when the resume alone cannot tell the full story.
details.whyItMatters: While some hiring managers skip cover letters, those who read them use them as a significant screening factor. A compelling cover letter can move you from the maybe pile to the interview list.
takeaways: Cover letters explain the why behind your application that resumes cannot
They demonstrate written communication skills and cultural fit signals
A strong cover letter differentiates you from equally qualified candidates

faq.question: Do hiring managers actually read cover letters in today's hiring process?
faq.answer: Surveys show that about sixty percent of hiring managers still consider cover letters important, with variation by industry and seniority. In fields like marketing, communications, and executive roles, they carry more weight..

faq.question: What makes a cover letter compelling enough to actually influence a hiring decision?
faq.answer: A compelling cover letter connects your specific experience to the company's specific challenges, demonstrates genuine knowledge of the organization, and reveals personality that a resume cannot convey. Generic templates fail because they lack the specificity that makes cover letters valuable.
